message.content: {"summary":"Your preliminary report presents a compelling Australian reef-monitoring mission with clear motivation, identified users, a detailed week-by-week Gantt chart and cited sources. Presentation is strong. To reach the top rubric levels, you need quantitative mission requirements, contingency planning in your schedule, and preliminary technical results — such as orbit or coverage analysis — rather than progress limited to tutorials and background reading.","next_steps":["Define quantitative mission requirements (spatial resolution, revisit time, swath, spectral bands) and link each to user needs, then discuss feasibility of seafloor-colour bleaching detection.","Add contingency provisions to your Gantt chart (e.g., buffer weeks, fallback strategies for launch/orbit trade-offs) and justify schedule risks in the context of the mission.","Produce and interpret at least one preliminary technical result in STK — e.g., a candidate orbit with coverage/revisit analysis — to substantiate the 'STK Simulations' weeks 4–10 plan and your near-real-time relay claim."],"criteria":{"C1":"Your Mission Concept & Rationale clearly motivates the mission, identifies marine and conservation scientists as users, and cites relevant literature (e.g., Asner's Hawaii system). To reach Accomplished, state explicit mission objectives and quantitative requirements — resolution, revisit time, coverage, spectral bands — and discuss feasibility of detecting seafloor-colour bleaching, since this implies demanding high-resolution multispectral imaging you have not yet addressed.","C2":"Your week-by-week Gantt chart with task descriptions tied to mission needs (launch, orbit, ground control, comms) and your sources list make the plan credible and feasible. For Accomplished, add provisions for variations and contingencies — schedule buffers, fallback options — and explain why the plan is structured this way in the context of the mission, including schedule risks such as the STK Simulations block spanning weeks 4–10.","C3":"Your progress so far — background reading, concept drafting and STK tutorials 1–4 — demonstrates only minor work. The Accomplished level requires a good preliminary set of results with brief interpretation: for example, candidate orbit parameters, coverage or revisit calculations, or link-budget hand calculations. Note your Gantt chart plans simulations but no simulation outputs are reported yet, which is inconsistent with the claimed progress.","C4":"Your report is well-written, logically structured with clear headings, consistent formatting, a labelled Gantt chart with legend, and footnote citations matching your reference list — well done. The one barrier to a higher mark is the 'Useful Links' section, which is not cited in the text. Integrate those sources into the body with proper in-text citations so all listed references are matched in both directions."}}
